This part takes the ADaM datasets built in this repository one step further.
It asks what a health technology assessment (HTA) would want from them.
An HTA body compares a new treatment with the treatments patients would
otherwise get. It wants effect measures with confidence intervals, subgroup
analyses and, when no head-to-head trial exists, indirect comparisons.

This is a self-study on public data. It is not part of any regulatory or HTA
submission, and the results support no claim about xanomeline.

## Chapters

1. **Time-to-event and safety analyses.** Kaplan-Meier, Cox models,
   proportional hazards, restricted mean survival time, subgroup analyses
   and effect measures for a binary safety endpoint. Data: ADSL, ADAE and
   ADTTE of the CDISC pilot study CDISCPILOT01, read from the committed
   transport files in `data/adam/`.
2. **Meta-analysis.** Fixed-effect and random-effects models, heterogeneity,
   forest and funnel plots, leave-one-out. Data: published trial results
   shipped with the `{metadat}` package.
3. **Indirect treatment comparison.** The Bucher method and a small network
   meta-analysis. Data: a published network shipped with `{netmeta}`.
   A text-only page on population-adjusted methods closes the chapter.

The [glossary](glossary.qmd) defines the HTA terms used throughout.

## How the numbers are checked

Every quantity that a chapter computes by hand is also computed with an
established package. A `testthat` test then checks that the two agree to
within 1e-8. The hand calculations live in `R/hta_methods.R`. The chapters
and the tests both use them, so the page and the test cannot drift apart.

No data are downloaded when this part is built. The CDISC pilot data come
from the transport files in the repository. The trial results come from
installed R packages.
